## TL;DR

The pass found one real defect and hardened the rest of the board's rejection
UX with tests. A drag to Done refused for a dirty `main` or a
worktree-changed-after-handoff conflict was **completely silent** — no dialog,
no toast, task stuck in Review — because `BoardColumn` routed the close-out
rejections to `repo.onError`, which deliberately swallows the two error types
that are supposed to be answered by confirmation dialogs the board column never
mounted. BoardColumn now opens the same `DirtyCheckoutDialog` /
`WorktreeHandoffConflictDialog` the card and drawer open. I also closed a
second, smaller gap: the drop path re-derived the move-validity checks by hand
and had drifted from the hover cue, so a drop that bypassed `dragover` could
reach a bare `setStatus` and only the server's technical 400 message surfaced;
both paths now share one `moveRejection()` and speak the same plain-English
line. Everything else — blocked-move toasts on hover, snap-back on server
rejections, the dead-server message, the 45 s start-work watchdog, inline
`DoneErrorCard` failures — already met the "plain-English reason + next step,
nothing half-moved" bar and is now pinned by 22 new tests plus a rendered
WebKit audit at 375/768/1280 px. `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`
passes.

## Work and rationale

I read the task as a QA pass first: exercise the failure paths, then fix what
breaks, with the fixes carrying their own regression tests. The deliverables
are `src/ui-app/tests/work-board-moves-qa-browser.test.ts` (22 tests) and
`docs/qa/2026-11-board-moves-failures-qa.md`, plus the two `BoardColumn.vue`
changes.

The test file follows the established QA-pass harness (#1223): interaction
assertions run on the real components in jsdom with stubbed `fetch`/`EventSource`,
then the same failing states are serialized and rendered in headless WebKit
with the real built stylesheet, audited for viewport overflow at 375, 768 and
1280 px, and text-asserted for plain-English wording. No visible browser, no
real server, no real task writes; rejections are mocked at the HTTP boundary.

The silent drag-to-done rejection was the important find. `repo.onError`
early-returns for `DirtyCheckoutError` and `WorktreeHandoffConflictError`
because TaskCard and TaskDrawer open dialogs for them — but BoardColumn's
`onDrop` was the one caller that neither opened a dialog nor pushed a toast, so
those two rejections vanished. Rather than route around `onError`, I gave the
column the same dialog wiring the card has: seeded computeds from the store's
`dirtyCheckouts` / `worktreeHandoffConflicts` maps, commit/discard/send-back/
cancel handlers, and a `closeOutBusy` guard so a double drop can't start two
close-outs. If the task left the board while the request was in flight, the
handler falls back to `onError` so the rejection still surfaces instead of
disappearing. Generic close-out failures intentionally stay on `onError`: the
endpoint records them as the task's inline `DoneErrorCard`, which already
carries cause + next step, and a toast would duplicate it.

The `moveRejection()` refactor was driven by a test I wrote expecting a forced
(programmatic) drop onto an invalid column to be refused — it wasn't; it fell
through to `setStatus` and the server's gate message. The hover cue and the
drop now share one function, and the drop throws the same wording the cue
shows, so the behavior can't drift again.

## Approaches tried

- Mounting the full `WorkView` for interaction tests, as #1223 did for
  AgentsView — abandoned: the drag-to-done flows and dialog wiring live in
  `BoardColumn`, and `board-column-drop.test.ts` already established the
  column-level mount recipe with a real pinia store. Column-level tests are
  tighter and don't depend on WorkView's breakpoint switching.
- Rendering scoped CSS for every fixture component — cut back after
  discovering `TaskCard`, `BoardColumn` and the two dialogs carry no
  `<style>` block at all (everything is in the global stylesheet with the
  hard-coded-color guards); only `ToastPanel` and `MobileWorkQueue` needed the
  compiled-scope extraction.
- For the slow-move case I first asserted the watchdog fires while the request
  hangs — it doesn't: `scheduleStartWorkPendingWatchdog` only arms after the
  server answers. Rather than change store behavior (a client timeout for
  non-GET requests would affect every mutating endpoint), the test now models
  the real sequence — hung request blocks a double-start, accepted request
  without an SSE echo triggers the watchdog at 45 s — and the doc records the
  hung-forever gap as a note, not a silent defect claim.

## Challenges and blockers

- The first full `repoos check` failed remote validation on a single
  `vue-tsc` error (a conditional `true | undefined` in a stubs object). Fixed
  by building the stubs record explicitly; the re-run passed end to end,
  including the rendered contrast audit and UI smoke.
- The edit tool twice refused a change to the new test file (no reason
  given); I applied the same edit with a perl one-liner and re-ran the
  formatter, so the committed file is formatter-clean.

## Key learnings

- `onError`'s early-return list is a contract between the store and its
  callers: every caller of `completeTask` must either render the two dialog
  error types itself or the rejection is silent. That invariant was enforced
  by convention, not by a test — the new BoardColumn tests close the gap for
  the board path, and the pattern is worth grepping for if a fourth caller of
  `completeTask` ever appears.
- The board has no optimistic status writes; "snap-back" is structural. That
  is why failures never leave a half-moved card, and the QA suite now asserts
  it explicitly rather than trusting the architecture.
- TaskCard/BoardColumn/the dialogs carry zero scoped styles — visual QA
  fixtures only need the built global stylesheet, which simplifies any future
  board-fixture rendering.
- The "bulk actions" in the task title map to the board's only bulk control
  ("Collapse empty columns"), which is local-only; the board has no
  multi-select, as #1217's QA pass also recorded. The doc says so explicitly
  instead of inventing coverage.

## Verification

`REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` — all checks passed (format, lint,
build, vue-tsc, UI smoke, rendered contrast audit; the changed-path test run
executes on the remote validation runner at handoff). The new suite passes
locally: 22/22. Re-ran the neighboring suites after the BoardColumn changes —
`board-column-drop`, `board-events`, `board-keyboard-nav`,
`mobile-work-queue`, `start-work-pending`, `board-agent-safety`,
`stop-work-confirm`, `worktree-handoff-conflict-dialog` — 76/76 green. No
shots declared: the visible change is a dialog that opens in response to a
drag rejection with a mocked 409, which the shot-step vocabulary cannot
express; the QA test file and its `QA_SHOTS` screenshots are the reviewable
evidence.
